'''Kamaljit Singh Bawa''', [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]] (born 7 April 1939 in Punjab, India) is an evolutionary ecologist, [[conservation biologist]] and a distinguished professor of Biology at the [[University of Massachusetts, Boston]].{{Citation needed|date=May 2025}} He is also the founder of [[Ashoka Trust for Research in Ecology and the Environment]]. In 2012, Bawa received the first [[Gunnerus Sustainability Award]], the world's major international award for work on sustainability.{{Citation needed|date=May 2025}} He is an elected member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web| url = http://www.amacad.org/news/pressReleaseContent.aspx?i=167| title = The History of Recent Science and Technology {{!}} American Academy of Arts and Sciences}}</ref> He was elected a Member of the [[American Philosophical Society]] in 2019.{{Citation needed|date=May 2025}}

==Academic career==
Bawa received B.S., M.S., and PhD degrees from [[Panjab University, Chandigarh]], India. After receiving his PhD in 1967, he came to the United States as a postdoctoral research associate and instructor at College of Forest Resources, [[University of Washington]]. He received the Maria Moors Cabot and the Charles Bullard Research Fellowships at [[Harvard University]] in 1972 and worked as a research fellow at the Grey Herbarium, Harvard University from 1973 to 1974.{{Citation needed|date=May 2025}} In 1974, he joined the Department of Biology, at [[University of Massachusetts, Boston]] as an assistant professor. He was promoted to associate professor in 1977 and to full professor in 1981 and became a distinguished professor in Biology in 1996 at the Department of Biology at [[University of Massachusetts, Boston]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Reference at www.umb.edu |url=http://www.umb.edu/academics/csm/faculty_staff/kamaljit_bawa/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120704023252/http://www.umb.edu/academics/csm/faculty_staff/kamaljit_bawa/ |archive-date=2012-07-04 |website=umb.edu}}</ref>

==Accolades and institutional affiliations==
{{Moresources|section|date=April 2024}}
[[Image:Kamal Bawa.jpg|thumbnail|right|200x200px|Kamal Bawa, 2012]]
Along with First [[Gunnerus Sustainability Award]],<ref>{{cite news| url = https://www.thehindu.com/sci-tech/energy-and-environment/kamal-bawa-gets-first-gunnerusaward-for-sustainability/article2903667.ece| title = Kamal Bawa gets first Gunnerus award for sustainability - The Hindu| newspaper = The Hindu| date = 17 February 2012}} </ref> Bawa is a recipient of the highest awards from the two main professional societies in his field. 

In 2003, the Association for Tropical Biology and Conservation bestowed on him its highest honour by electing him as an Honorary Fellow.{{Citation needed|date=May 2025}}  The [[Society for Conservation Biology]] awarded him its Distinguished Service Award in 2009. He also received P.N. Mehra Memorial Award in Botany in 2007.{{Citation needed|date=May 2025}}

Bawa has been a [[Guggenheim Fellow]] from 1987 to 1988 as well as a [[Pew Scholar]] in Conservation and the Environment from 1991 to 1996, a Giorgio Ruffolo Visiting Scholar in Sustainability Science in the Sustainability Science Program at Harvard's [[Center for International Development]],{{Citation needed|date=May 2025}} and a Bullard Fellow at the [[Harvard Forest]] in 1972,{{Citation needed|date=May 2025}} and again in 2009. He was an elected fellow for [[The National Academy of Sciences, India]] and the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] (AAAS), American Academy of Arts and Sciences,{{Citation needed|date=May 2025}} and the Royal Norwegian Society of Letters and Sciences.<ref>{{cite website| url = https://www.dknvs.no/akademiet/medlemmer/gruppe-iv-generell-biologi/| title = Gruppe IV  Generell biologi| publisher = Royal Norwegian Society of Sciences and Letters| accessdate = 3 August 2025}} </ref>

He served on NSF Advisory Panel on Conservation and Restoration Biology in 1991 and on population biology in 1993, 1994.{{Citation needed|date=May 2025}} He has also been a member of the Science Committee, DIVERSITAS-agrobiodiversity Group since 2006. He also serves on the advisory boards of [[Conabio]], Natureserve, TEAM Program of [[Conservation International]], William L. Brown Center of the [[Missouri Botanical Garden]].{{Citation needed|date=May 2025}} He is a member of the Board of Trustees of [[S M Sehgal Foundation]], previously named the Institute of Rural Research and Development (IRRAD), the Foundation for Revitalization of Local Health Traditions, and the Committee for Research and Exploration of the [[National Geographic Society]].<ref>{{cite web| url = https://www.nationalgeographic.org/society/grants-and-investments/| title = Grants and Investments - National Geographic Society| website = [[National Geographic Society]]}}</ref>

Bawa is the president of the [https://www.atree.org Ashoka Trust for Research in Ecology and Environment (ATREE)], a non-governmental organisation devoted to research, policy analysis, and education in India,<ref>{{cite web |title=Reference at www.atree.org |url=http://www.atree.org/governing_board |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100211003337/http://www.atree.org/governing_board |archive-date=2010-02-11 |website=atree.org}}</ref> member of the governing boards of the Institute of Ayurveda and Integrative Medicine, and Village Forward.

== Awards and honors ==
In 2012 Bawa received the international [[Gunnerus Sustainability Award]], presented by the Royal Norwegian Society of Science and Letters.<ref>{{cite web| url = https://www.dknvs.no/gunnerusprisen/gunnerus-award/2012-laureate-kamal-bawa/?lang=en | title = 2012 Laureate – Kamal Bawa | accessdate = 3 August 2025 | publisher = The Royal Norwegian Society of Science and Letters}} </ref>

Bawa was elected as a [[List of Fellows of the Royal Society elected in 2015|Fellow of the Royal Society (FRS) in 2015]].<ref>{{cite web| url = http://gonitsora.com/kamal-bawa-and-ajay-sood-elected-frs/| title = Kamal Bawa and Ajay Sood elected FRS - Gonit Sora| date = May 2015}}</ref>

In 2016, he was awarded the Jose [[Cuatrecasas Medal for Excellence in Tropical Botany]].<ref name="ATREE2016">{{cite web |title=Shoots and Leaves - Accolades |url=https://www.atree.org/newsletters/shoots_leaves/june_2016/shoots_leaves_june_2016_2.html |website=ATREE |publisher=ATREE Trust |accessdate=23 April 2020}}</ref>

==Publications==
Bawa has authored more than 180 academic papers, author or editor of ten books, monographs or special issues of journals including ''Sahayadris: India’s Western Ghats – A Vanishing Heritage''.{{Citation needed|date=May 2025}} He is the editor-in-chief of ''[[Conservation and Society]]'', an interdisciplinary journal in conservation; associate editor of ''[[Ecology and Society]]''; and academic editor of ''[[PLoS ONE]]''.{{Citation needed|date=May 2025}} He is a member of the editorial board of ''Journal of Sustainable Forestry''. He was an associate editor of ''Conservation Biology'' from 1987 to 1993. He served on the editorial board of ''Journal of Arnold Arboretum'' from 1986 to 1990, ''Journal of Tree Science'' from 1986 to 1991, and ''Evolutionary Trends in Plants'' from 1987 to 1992.{{Citation needed|date=May 2025}}
